questions.stem: The diagram shows a Bunsen burner.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The Bunsen burner uses methane as a fuel. Methane has the formula $ \mathrm{C H_{4}} $ Give the names of the two elements in methane.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When methane burns it reacts with a gas in the air. Give the name of this gas.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the two substances that form when methane burns in plenty of air.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Name the poisonous gas that forms when methane burns in a shortage of air.

questions.stem: A student uses this apparatus to investigate the burning of four different liquid fuels, W, X, Y and Z. The table shows the student's results.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the table by giving the increase in temperature for fuels X, Y and Z.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The student uses the same mass of water and burns each fuel for the same period of time. Explain which fuel releases the most heat energy.

parts.label: c
parts.text: What is the name given to reactions that release heat energy? A decomposition B endothermic C exothermic D reduction

questions.stem: A student makes an alkali solution by dissolving a small volume of cleaning liquid in deionised water. He then titrates a sample of this solution with an acid until neutralisation is complete.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diagram shows the burette readings for his titration. Use the readings to complete the table, giving all values to the nearest 0.05 $ cm^{3}. $

parts.label: b
parts.text: Another student does a titration using a solution of a different cleaning liquid. The table shows her results. Concordant results are those that differ by $ 0. 2 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ or less.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Place ticks in the table to show which results are concordant.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Use the concordant results to calculate the average (mean) volume of acid added.

questions.stem: Bromine, chlorine, fluorine and iodine are elements in Group 7 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which element is the most reactive? A bromine B chlorine D iodine C fluorine

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which element is a solid at room temperature? A bromine B chlorine C fluorine D iodine

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which element has the darkest colour at room temperature? A bromine B chlorine C fluorine D iodine

parts.text: Bromine reacts with hydrogen to form hydrogen bromide. Use the values in the table to calculate the enthalpy change for the reaction between hydrogen and bromine.

questions.stem: Ethanol can be manufactured by fermentation or by the direct hydration of ethene.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In Brazil, the main source of sugar for fermentation is sugar cane. sugar cane is added to water sugar cane contains sucrose $ \left( \mathrm{C}_{1 2} \mathrm{H}_{2 2} \mathrm{O}_{1 1} \right) $ that dissolves in the water during the fermentation process the sucrose is broken down into glucose $ \left( \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{1 2} \mathrm{O}_{6} \right) $ this glucose is then converted into ethanol （ $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{5} O H} $ ）and carbon dioxide

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: Name the substance that is added to the sucrose solution to allow fermentation to take place.

parts.label: a-ii

parts.label: a-iii
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the conversion of glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

parts.label: a-iv
parts.text: Fermentation produces a solution that is a mixture of ethanol and water. Which of these is the most effective method of obtaining ethanol from this mixture? A crystallisation B filtration C fractional distillation D simple distillation

parts.label: b
parts.text: In the direct hydration method, ethene reacts with steam. The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {4} + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {C} _ {2} \mathrm {H} _ {5} \mathrm {O H}$

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Name the catalyst used in this reaction.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: State the temperature and pressure used in this reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: This apparatus is used to convert ethanol into ethene.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Name the type of reaction taking place.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State the function of the aluminium oxide in this reaction.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Ethene belongs to a homologous series of unsaturated hydrocarbons called alkenes.

parts.label: d-i

questions.stem: Phosgene $ \left( \mathrm{C O C I}_{2} \right) $ is used in industry to make polymers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Phosgene is formed when carbon monoxide reacts with chlorine. $\mathrm {C O} (\mathrm {g}) + \mathrm {C I} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm {C O C I} _ {2} (\mathrm {g}) \quad \Delta H = - 1 0 8 \mathrm {k J / m o l}$

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: The reaction mixture is kept at temperatures between 50 and $ 1 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ If a temperature above $ 2 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ is used, only a small amount of phosgene is formed. Suggest why only a small amount of phosgene is formed at temperatures above 200 $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Predict how the yield of phosgene will change if the reaction is carried out at a higher pressure. Give a reason for your answer. [assume the reaction reaches a position of equilibrium]

parts.label: b
parts.text: Phosgene reacts with water to form hydrochloric acid and carbon dioxide. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The diagram shows the displayed formula of phosgene. Draw a dot and cross diagram to show the arrangement of all the outer electrons in a molecule of phosgene.

questions.stem: Magnesium carbonate decomposes when heated to form magnesium oxide and carbon dioxide. The equation for the reaction is $\mathrm {M g C O} _ {3} (\mathrm {s}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g O} (\mathrm {s}) + \mathrm {C O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$ Step1 weigh a clean, dry crucible and record the mass Step 2 add some magnesium carbonate Step 3 reweigh the crucible and contents and record the new mass Step 4 heat the crucible and contents for five minutes Step 5 allow the crucible and contents to cool and then reweigh Step 6 repeat steps 4 and 5 until the mass of the crucible and contents does not change The student does the experiment four times. The table shows her results. A student uses this method to investigate the reaction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State why the mass of the crucible and contents decreases during heating.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the reason for Step 6.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Explain in which experiment the student should have heated for a fourth period of five minutes.

questions.stem: Acid indigestion is caused by having too much hydrochloric acid in the stomach. The equation for the reaction between magnesium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid is $\mathrm {M g} (\mathrm {O H}) _ {2} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {H C l} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g C l} _ {2} (\mathrm {a q}) + 2 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {I})$ He uses 0.29g of magnesium hydroxide to neutralise the hydrochloric acid. A student investigates how much magnesium hydroxide is needed to neutralise $ 1 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of hydrochloric acid with a concentration of $ 0. 0 9 6 8 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3}. $

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of HCl in the hydrochloric acid. amount of HCl

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the amount, in moles, of $ \mathrm{M g(OH)}_{2} $ used by the student. $ [M_{r} $ of $ \mathrm{M g(OH)}_{2}=5 8] $ $\mathrm {M g} (\mathrm {O H}) _ {2}$

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain whether the student used the right amount of magnesium hydroxide to neutralise the hydrochloric acid.
